description: Master provenance manifest for all network device configuration sources discovered during the dataset acquisition campaign. Every entry is independently verified for provenance.

notes.verified_real_production: 10 Internet2 backbone router configs from Config2Spec repository. These are real Internet2 JunOS configs with some lines removed for Batfish parsing. The Purdue ISL campus dataset (~1600 Cisco configs) exists but requires academic request and is not yet acquired.
notes.honest_assessment: The vast majority of publicly accessible network device configurations are synthetic, lab-generated, or official vendor examples. Real production configs are extremely scarce due to security sensitivity. The NetCloak paper (2025) explicitly confirms: 'most evaluation datasets for network configurations are synthesized, while real-world configurations are scarce due to privacy concerns.'

datasets_discovered.name: Config2Spec Internet2 Backbone Configs
provenance_evidence: README explicitly states: 'With the exception of Internet2, the configs have been synthesized using NetComplete' - distinguishing Internet2 as real

Router names match real Internet2 PoP locations: ATLA=Atlanta, CHIC=Chicago, CLEV=Cleveland, HOUS=Houston, KANS=Kansas City, LOSA=Los Angeles, NEWY=New York, SALT=Salt Lake City, SEAT=Seattle, WASH=Washington DC
Config contains real Internet2 IP addresses (64.57.x.x, 198.32.x.x), real RADIUS servers, real BGP peer addresses
References to real Internet2 peers: CzechLight/VINI, FranceTelecom mcast, NLR-TELEPRESENCE
Published as part of USENIX NSDI'20 paper by ETH Zurich NSG group
JunOS version 12.3R6.6 is consistent with Internet2 infrastructure timeframe
datasets_discovered.modifications: Some lines removed for Batfish/Minesweeper parsing compatibility. Community matches, empty prefix-list matches, and certain route-map entries removed.
datasets_discovered.sensitive_data_warning: Contains real Internet2 IP addresses, RADIUS server addresses, and BGP peer information. These are from a research/education backbone and are semi-public infrastructure, but sanitization should be applied before redistribution.
datasets_discovered.acquisition_notes: Acquired, cryptographically verified against nsg-ethz/config2spec original repository, sanitized, and stored under dataset/real_device_evaluation/. Excluded from training splits to prevent data leakage.

datasets_discovered.name: Purdue ISL Campus Network Configuration Snapshot
provenance_evidence: Dataset page states: 'running configuration files from all devices' across 'about 1600 Cisco routers and switches' from 'a large campus network'
Referenced in published research: Sung, Rao, Xie, Maltz (2008 CoNEXT paper)
Hosted by Purdue University Internet Systems Lab with formal academic data request process
Data described as anonymized for privacy protection
Maintained at https://engineering.purdue.edu/~isl/network-config/ since at least 2008
datasets_discovered.acquisition_notes: Requires academic data request at https://engineering.purdue.edu/~isl/network-config/data.html. Requestor must provide: name, school email, institution, personal webpage, intended use. Data restricted to academic research only. Must cite 2008 CoNEXT paper. Dataset is ~5MB zip file from November 2008 snapshot.

datasets_discovered.name: Azure VPN Gateway Device Configuration Samples
provenance_evidence: Repository description: 'VPN configuration samples contributed by the community'
README describes these as 'samples' that have been 'validated by the community'
All configs contain placeholder IP addresses (206.X.X.X, 40.X.X.X) with redacted octets
Juniper SRX config contains impossible timestamp (month '0X'), confirming template nature
Hostname is generic 'Azure_SRX' / 'Azure_ASA' etc.
datasets_discovered.acquisition_notes: Publicly accessible on GitHub. These are reference templates, not real device exports. Useful for parser development and vendor syntax coverage but NOT real-device evidence.

datasets_discovered.name: Palo Alto Networks Iron-Skillet Day-One Templates
provenance_evidence: Published by PaloAltoNetworks official GitHub organization
Described as 'day one best practice configuration templates'
Templates for NGFW and Panorama
datasets_discovered.acquisition_notes: Publicly accessible. Official vendor best-practice templates. Good for PAN-OS parser development.

datasets_discovered.name: Kentik Network Device Configuration Snippets
provenance_evidence: Published by Kentik (network observability company)
Config snippets for customers to configure flow/SNMP/BGP export to Kentik platform
Partial configurations (not full running-config), focused on telemetry setup
datasets_discovered.acquisition_notes: Partial configs only (snippets, not full device configs). Useful for vendor syntax coverage.

datasets_discovered.name: Freifunk Berlin Backbone Node Configs
provenance_evidence: README states these manage 'OpenWrt mesh nodes in the city-wide backbone of Freifunk Berlin'
Freifunk Berlin is a well-known community wireless mesh network serving the city of Berlin
Ansible-managed configs for named locations (derrida, tberg-core, refugee-mesh, etc.)
datasets_discovered.acquisition_notes: These are Ansible playbook configs for OpenWRT, not traditional CLI configs (Cisco IOS, JunOS etc.). Limited utility for NetAudit's vendor-specific parser training, but valuable as verified real-device examples of network configuration.

datasets_discovered.name: DN42/Internet AS Configuration (myzhang1029)
provenance_evidence: Repository title: 'Internet configuration files for AS4242420893, AS211585, and related devices (publicly released part)'
Contains real AS numbers for dn42 and Internet routing
'publicly released part' implies sensitive parts removed from real operational configs
datasets_discovered.acquisition_notes: BIRD2/nftables configs for Linux routing. DN42 is a real decentralized network but is an overlay/hobbyist network. Configs use BIRD syntax, not traditional vendor CLI.

datasets_discovered.name: DN42 Router Configs (n0toose)
provenance_evidence: README states: configs are 'used by myself for my own, personal dn42 router'
DN42 is a real decentralized network with real BGP peering
datasets_discovered.acquisition_notes: Personal dn42 router configs. BIRD/Linux routing, not traditional vendor CLI.

datasets_not_publicly_accessible.name: Stanford University Backbone Network Configs
datasets_not_publicly_accessible.provenance_evidence: Used in Batfish (NSDI 2015) and Header Space Analysis research. 16 Cisco routers from Stanford's actual production backbone.
datasets_not_publicly_accessible.access: Not publicly released. Configs used internally for research only.
datasets_not_publicly_accessible.confidence: HIGH for existence, NONE for public availability

datasets_not_publicly_accessible.name: Georgia Tech + UW-Madison Campus Configs
datasets_not_publicly_accessible.provenance_evidence: IMC 2011 paper: 'The Evolution of Network Configuration: A Tale of Two Campuses'. 5 years of RANCID-collected config snapshots.
datasets_not_publicly_accessible.access: Not publicly released as downloadable dataset.
datasets_not_publicly_accessible.confidence: HIGH for existence, LOW for public availability

datasets_not_publicly_accessible.name: Microsoft Research Anonymized Carrier Configs
datasets_not_publicly_accessible.provenance_evidence: Paper: 'Protecting Router Configuration by Outsourcing Anonymization'. 7600+ routers across 31 networks from a major carrier, anonymized using structure-preserving methods.
datasets_not_publicly_accessible.access: Not publicly downloadable. Requires contacting Microsoft Research / CMU authors.
datasets_not_publicly_accessible.confidence: HIGH for existence, LOW for public availability

datasets_not_publicly_accessible.name: PreConfig Network Configuration Corpus
datasets_not_publicly_accessible.provenance_evidence: ArXiv paper 2403.09369. Data extracted from vendor manuals and community forums, not from real devices directly.
datasets_not_publicly_accessible.access: Dataset availability unclear. Contact paper authors.
